families.actual_work: Isolated worker change in the completed initial 144 paired-job factor matrix; 24 earlier full Playground games (8 seeds × auto32/explicit4/affinity-auto6), plus separate fresh 16 Playground and 8 Oazis participant-count games.
families.code: Affinity-aware auto participant discovery implemented and retained; explicit counts preserved.
families.outcome: Largest underreported accepted fix: auto32→auto6 within six eligible logical CPUs reduced whole-process CPU 46.98%, wall34.25%, RSS14.32% in ten-layout initial matrix. Fixed-three negative control essentially flat. Earlier eight-seed full Playground affinity-auto6 CPU29.81% and whole elapsed18.16% lower.
families.decision: Accepted general eligible-CPU ceiling; no global optimum3, no unrestricted-host speed promise.
families.reopen_criteria: Reopen for affinity/quota correctness on additional operating systems or coordinator allocations, not a universal three-thread optimum. Compare speed and throughput under the same total budget.

families.actual_work: 48 native timed windows/24 pairs at N4/N6/auto32 plus16 windows/8 pairs at N3; twelve separate full8192-tick control traces. Later ten-layout preferred-participant factor and mature factor controls.
families.outcome: Benefits strongest in oversubscribed auto32; at N3 Playground wall+0.16%,CPU+0.34%; Oazis wall−1.17%,CPU−1.16%. N4/N6 mixed.
families.decision: Rejected for final source; extra scheduling policy did not justify complexity after fixing allocation.
families.reopen_criteria: Only revisit with measured runnable eligibility/notification contention at sensible allocations and a simpler explicit readiness design; do not repeat unconditional wake tweaks assuming the oversubscribed gain generalizes.

families.actual_work: Initial eager reclamation factor;96-job mature factor matrix;44 snapshot-V2 jobs inside completed68-job follow-up (20 initial,24 mature/direct comparison jobs).
families.code: Eager unleased-descriptor cleanup then lazy pressure-based tryAcquire/reclaim implemented separately.
families.outcome: Negligible independent memory benefit; mixed CPU, small-Nicowar/Oazis slowdowns, adverse Playground GPU-on wall result.
families.decision: Both ownership candidates rolled back; original simpler ownership retained with optional query-only census.
families.reopen_criteria: Do not reimplement eager/lazy reclamation unchanged. First account for published, staged, paused search and retained capacities; show an independent memory win without extra CPU.

families.actual_work: Earlier reserve prototype16 GPU-on+16 CPU-off windows and32 fresh confirmation windows; initial V1 factor, mature V1/V2 comparisons;24 selected fresh paired jobs (21 V2/fresh baseline plus3 V1 large-mixed), with three large-mixed seeds and six counterbalanced pairs each.
families.code: Lossless immutable descriptor schema and compact numeric values; V2 reuses matching prior schema/one-find lookup without wire changes.
families.outcome: Initial V2 RSS10.8–37.5% lower across ten layouts; mature Playground about22–23% lower GPU-off and13% GPU-on, Oazis11%/8–9%. Adverse mature PG GPU-on direct V2/V1 CPU+2.015% retained; V1 original large-mixed CPU signal did not recur at same size.
families.decision: V2 accepted with exact outputs/replay/lifetime gates; no universal speed claim.
families.reopen_criteria: Retain lossless V2; target proven remaining schema/value duplication. Recheck mature GPU-on overhead and complete byte-for-byte output/lifetime gates.

families.actual_work: Actual first-quarantine event observer, device/pacing controls;14 paired timing jobs for host synchronization,39 recovery-vs-sync jobs; actual hardware cancellation/reap/fresh-field and scalar material/clear/guard oracle cases.
families.code: Required host synchronization retained; recovery prototype implemented, exercised on real GPU and rejected.
families.outcome: Startup GPU contexts cost roughly114–116MiB while useful completion low; recovery increased committed GPU fields but added CPU and wall cost across varied workloads.
families.decision: Keep synchronization correctness and permanent-failure safe CPU fallback; reject recovery as optimization.
families.reopen_criteria: Do not adopt retry recovery merely to increase participation. Reopen around useful batch size, transfer volume and publication deadlines, measuring total CPU/wall/RSS and useful commits.

families.actual_work: 24 native table/lazy/full windows (two maps×two seeds×two repeats×three variants), separate exact8192-tick traces.
families.code: Existing depth execution controls exercised; no replacement adopted.
families.outcome: Lazy Playground wall+5.39%,CPU+0.42%; Oazis wall+4.09%,CPU−3.23%. Full Playground wall−2.76%,CPU+1.49%; Oazis wall−0.48%,CPU+9.58%.
families.decision: No universal switch: lower computed-work counters did not ensure faster completion.
families.reopen_criteria: Profile-specific latency/CPU choices may be valid after multi-device evidence; no global lazy/full switch follows from these two-map controls.

families.actual_work: 16 native malloc-arena cases;24 pool cap0/16/64 cases; symbolic heap ownership controls.
families.code: Isolated configuration/control variants, retained-cap admission controls.
families.outcome: Arena cap tiny RSS reduction (<1.2%) with CPU generally higher. Pool0 reduced PG RSS2.39% but CPU+1.86%, wall+1.60%; Oazis mixed. Heap showed removal raised total requested allocation and calls.
families.decision: No arena global cap or wholesale pool removal adopted.
families.reopen_criteria: Target actual ownership and capacity, not global arena caps or deleting all pools. Require measured allocation-call and CPU cost alongside RSS.

families.actual_work: Eight same-release native Sep11 windows, original/clone/on/off exact traces.
families.outcome: Autosave-off CPU and wall31.36% lower in that historical workload.
families.decision: Explains cost; not accepted optimization because autosave must remain. Current serialization optimization not established by this probe.
families.reopen_criteria: Optimize serialization or repeated preparation while retaining autosave. Feature-off savings are a diagnostic upper bound, not an accepted capability removal.

families.actual_work: Two corrected historical dispatch cohorts:28 controls+16 native timing runs, common torus corrections, reached-field oracle and cross-binary traces.
families.code: Historical isolated dispatch replacement, not current feature rollback.
families.outcome: Chamfer/BFS CPU ratios2.57/3.10 for transitional policy (PG/Oazis),2.29/2.73 with cap256.
families.decision: Causal historical dispatch cost demonstrated; cannot attribute whole historical interval or infer current replacement.
families.reopen_criteria: Use historical control to understand the transition, not to revert current gradient rules. Any new dispatch must preserve actual current scalar outputs/publication ticks.

families.actual_work: Exact #341 parent-kernel TU replacement:16 native windows plus22 microprocesses over18 synthetic fixtures; full PG8192 trace.
families.code: Historical parent/current comparison, no additional newly adopted optimization.
families.outcome: Existing optimized kernel CPU/wall about22.4% lower PG and20.6% lower Oazis.
families.decision: Confirmed prior optimization payoff, not fresh48h shipping speedup.
families.reopen_criteria: Prior payoff was confirmed; do not count it as a newly discovered optimization. Current kernel remains baseline for future disassembly and oracle-verified proposals.

families.actual_work: Six Sep29 AI1/4×gradient0/1/2 exact trace controls and24 native windows with same eight-tick publication.
families.outcome: AI1/grad0 wall+16.44%,CPU−14.75% vs AI4/grad2; AI1/grad2 wall−0.51%,CPU−6.93%.
families.decision: Established CPU/latency tradeoff, not general current default policy.
families.reopen_criteria: Investigate resource-profile tradeoffs under unchanged AI decisions and eight-tick publication; CPU savings and completion latency can conflict.

families.actual_work: 540 verified warm K1 timings across18 fixtures and750 K3 timings across25 fixtures, independent field output and visitation oracle evidence.
families.code: Isolated chunk16/128 and public FIFO batching32/128 prototypes.
families.outcome: Chunk128 sometimes~1.5% faster but one256² fixture~30.3% slower with more capacity. FIFO alternatives all25 median CPU/wall regress,24/25 intervals entirely adverse.
families.decision: Rejected both general replacements; keep current64 and current FIFO. Warm kernel microbench only, not mature game evidence.
families.reopen_criteria: Do not repeat fixed16/128 chunks or batching32/128 as blanket replacement. Reopen only with a new work/granularity model and fixture-specific explanation for regressions.

families.actual_work: Initial whole-game Callgrind, symbolized natural-winner Oazis heap; attempted one-hour mature Callgrind. Later accepted-source continuous native perf is audited separately by root.
families.code: Diagnostics/source ownership audit rather than optimization.
families.outcome: Mature heap peak521,535,011 requested bytes: gradient fields130.8MB,snapshots93.3MB,search frontiers74.1MB,replay55.2MB. Mature Callgrind timed out before target START/STOP and produced no valid mature attribution.
families.decision: Useful ownership priorities; failed one-hour instrumented attempt is real effort but no result. New cache invalidation/ownership redesign remains unimplemented.
families.reopen_criteria: New ownership/invalidation census and continuous late-game profiles are still useful. One-hour Callgrind timed out before target and supplies no valid mature attribution.
